user_questions.question: Before I build the inventory, three choices change what gets built: (1) What identifies a 'merchant case'? Options: (a) Case.Type = 'Merchant Operations' (picklist value exists, 0 cases today; no Case record types), (b) any case with Storefront__c set, (c) cases whose Business_Account__c is a Partner_Account record type. (2) Which queue? (a) create a new Case queue 'Merchant Support Queue' (no Case-enabled queue exists; Merchant_Messaging_Queue serves MessagingSession only), or (b) add Case to Merchant_Messaging_Queue. (3) What counts as a 'response' that stops the 2-hour escalation? (a) first outbound agent email or case comment, (b) status change away from New, (c) owner accepting the case. Also confirm all parts of the request (link, auto-fill, route, escalate, LWC) are in scope.
user_questions.simulated_answer: All five parts are in scope. 'Response' = first agent email or comment. Merchant case definition and queue: No preference; use your recommended default.

skill_friction: The askcoworker-calls.md note says R and T can be combined for eight changes or fewer at 500 words; the combined call for a 7-change inventory timed out at ~61s, and the retry had to split R and T. The combined option seems unreliable.

Rule 3 says reject proposals that contradict documented Salesforce behavior, but provides no allowed way to check documentation; two AskCoworker claims (scheduled paths fire at fixed clock times and cannot be cancelled; before-save flows cannot use Get Records) were rejected based on model knowledge only. The skill does not say how to tag such a rejection.

org-verification.md implies MetadataComponentDependency finds readers of a field, but it returned 0 rows for Case.Storefront__c and Case.Business_Account__c even though Apex bodies reference them; absence checks must use Apex body scans too, which the guidance could state explicitly.

Assignment rule entries and escalation rules cannot be read with the allowed commands (Tooling EscalationRule unsupported); the skill has no guidance for automation that can override a proposed change but cannot be inspected.
Module guidance ('known force-app path or Not specified') is ambiguous when the force-app/main/default subdirectories exist but are empty and the needed subdirectory (flows) does not exist.
AskCoworker repeatedly tagged facts as 'Verified: prior session' (e.g. DataStreamDefinition = 0) despite the ignore-earlier-conversations header; each needed re-verification, adding query overhead.

Step 5 lets the scope message carry up to 3 questions, but the simulated user's intent covered only one of the three forks, so two answers fell back to defaults; fine per RUNNER, but the skill does not say whether defaults chosen after a 'no preference' answer are tagged user decision or assumption.
Runner error on my side: in the I call I tagged '2 calendar hours' as a user decision although it was a default; corrected in the spec (Section 8 item 6 marks it an assumption).
